messages:
olivia: Pushed an nsys capture for the 8-concurrent-req workload. initial takeaway: KV-related kernels dominate inclusive time, but perfetto shows different active SM patterns. Can we walk and rank hotspots?

kai: Got the trace link from infra-bot. quick snapshot from `nsys stats` I ran locally: 
```
Top kernels by inclusive time:
1) kv_cache_lookup_kernel         42.1%  1208.3 ms
2) fused_attention_forward        28.6%   822.7 ms
3) softmax_block_reduction         12.3%   354.1 ms
4) kv_cache_update_kernel          6.0%   169.2 ms
5) memcpy H2D                      3.4%    95.8 ms
6) token_postproc                  2.6%    72.2 ms
```
(This is inclusive time from the CUDA kernel table)

sam: Interesting — kv_cache_lookup is absurdly high. On perfetto the kernel timeline shows many short launches overlapping and a lot of idle gaps on SMs between them. sm_efficiency looks low for those small kernels.

maria: Can you paste the CUPTI metrics? I want `sm_efficiency`, `achieved_occupancy`, and `gld_throughput` per-kernel.

kai: Ran a metrics pass (small sample):
```
kv_cache_lookup_kernel: sm_efficiency=24%, achieved_occupancy=0.18, gld_throughput=6.2GB/s
fused_attention_forward: sm_efficiency=79%, achieved_occupancy=0.82, gld_throughput=18.9GB/s
softmax_block_reduction: sm_efficiency=45%, achieved_occupancy=0.36, gld_throughput=4.1GB/s
kv_cache_update_kernel: sm_efficiency=30%, achieved_occupancy=0.22, gld_throughput=7.3GB/s
```

olivia: That matches what I saw — many tiny KV lookups chew wall time because of kernel launch overhead + poor occupancy. They show high inclusive time because they serialize across streams even though they should be fused/batched.

sam: For ranking: if we compute token-normalized cost (ms per token) kv_lookup is ~0.38 ms/token, attention ~0.12 ms/token. So KV is first candidate.

maria: Potential fixes: 1) batch multiple KV lookups into a single kernel (reduce launch overhead), 2) change memory layout to coalesce loads (improve gld_throughput), 3) increase threads/block to improve occupancy for small batches, or 4) run micro-batching inside kernel.

olivia: Also noticed `fused_attention_forward` uses cutlass and is well-optimized — leave it as is but we can try a lighter quantized variant for tail requests. Primary perf regressions after the recent change appear correlated with a refactor in the KV indexing code (see diff 8f3a).

kai: Repro steps I used: 
```bash
nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=none -o trace_8req python serve_perf.py --batch-size 8 --model redwood-v1
# then metrics export
nsys stats trace_8req.qdrep --report=cupti_metrics --metrics sm_efficiency,achieved_occupancy,gld_throughput -o metrics.csv
```

maria: Good. I'll try a micro-batch KV kernel and run with `--batch-size 16` to see break-even. If occupancy goes up and inclusive time drops, we prove launch overhead is the issue.

infra-bot: Trace uploaded: https://artifacts.internal.redwood/traces/1769003456/trace_8req.qdrep :thumbsup:

sam: Quick note: also check context-switches and CPU-to-GPU serialization in perfetto — some of those gaps are blocked by async memcpy scheduling. Could be overlapping issues.

olivia: Thanks — maria, please paste results when you have metrics. I'll open a short PR outline for KV batching and a perf-run checklist.

maria: Will do, aiming for a new trace by EOD.
